newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bank bill yields ease after TWI recovers.
newsitem.headline: NZ bank bill yields ease after TWI recovers.

text.p: New Zealand bank bill yields, which had risen in the morning, eased back in the afternoon as the currency regained strength.
"The market has been motivated by nothing more than the dollar," a Wellington bank dealer said.
He said that because Treasurer Winston Peters and Finance Minister Bill Birch said nothing about wanting the Kiwi dollar lower, it was good enough for the Kiwi to rally.
And that was the signal for the bank bills to recoup some of their lost ground.
However, it was a trader-driven rally and the market remains stuck in a narrow range between 7.60 percent and 7.70 percent.
Bond yields were marked higher in the morning mainly as a result of short-end weakness and stuck there most of the session.
Dealers said there was light buying in the 00, 02 and 04 bonds towards the end of the day but the market is essentially treading water ahead of the Reserve Bank six monthly projections on Thursday.
The bond market took little note of comments from Peters and Birch, with a trader noting that the "Reserve Bank are their own masters".

The market is evenly divided on what line the RB will take, with half expecting the bank to take note of the effects the strong currency is having on the tradeable sector and the other half seeing the bank wanting higher interest rates to stifle inflation.
